textbookText: b. Chlamydospores: They are formed during unfavourable condition. The protoplasm of hyphae collects at certain places, rounds off accumulates a lot of food materials and develops a thick wall to form chlamydospores. During favourable condition, these chlamydospores germinate to form new mycelium.
c. Oidia: Hyphae of certain Mucor when growing in a liquid medium

rich in sugar, become septate. Then septate cells round
off to form reproductive structures called oidia. They take
part in fermentation and multiply by budding like yeast. When taken to
solid medium, oidia produce new mycelia.
3. Sexual Reproduction:
Figure 2.4.8 Oidia
Sexual reproduction in Mucor takes place by conjugation (i.e. gametangial copulation) during
unfavourable conditions. It takes place between the mycelia of two different mating types (i.e.
heterothallic).
During sexual reproduction, two opposite stains of hyphae i.e. +ve strain and –ve strain come
close together and develop short club-shaped protuberances called progametangia. They come
in contact at the tip and septum appears in each progametangium that divides it into a basal
suspensor and a terminal gametangium. After sometime, the contact walls of the two
gametangia dissolve and two gametes fuse together to form zygote having number of diploid

nuclei. The process is called conjugation. The zygote grows in size, become rounded and secretes a wall and this structure is known as zygospore. The zygospore undergoes a resting for a while. It has dense cytoplasm containing a number of diploid nuclei, cell organelles and food reserve. After resting period, the zygospore germinates. Out of many diploid nuclei of zygospore only one is functional. This functional nucleus divides by meiosis into four haploid nuclei, among them three degenerate and one divides many times to form many nuclei of same strain. The protoplast of zygospore swells up, ruptures outer wall and comes out in the form of a vertical germ-tube, called promycelium. The tip of promycelium swells up and forms rounded germ sporangium which produces non-motile, uninucleate, haploid germspores. The germ spores are liberated and on suitable substratum, they germinate to form new mycelium.
Figure 2.4.9 Life cycle of Mucor Activity 2.2: To observe the Mucor growth on bread.
Material Required: 1. Bread slice 2. Plastic bag 3. Clear tape 4. Water 5. Magnifying glass or Microscope Procedure:

• Damp the bread with few drops of water. • Place the damp bread in plastic bag and seal with tape. • Place the bag in a warm area out of direct sunlight. • Observe it daily until Mucor is seen. • Use magnifying glasses or microscope (taking few threads from this mould
